newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-U.S. unfair trade call disappointing - Canberra.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-U.S. unfair trade call disappointing - Canberra.

text.p: The Australian government said on Wednesday it was disappointed at a United States decision to include Australia's textile clothing and footwear and passenger motor vehicles industry schemes in its unfair trade practices investigations.

"We are very disappointed in this step by the United States and will vigorously defend the (industry) schemes and Australian industry interests against challenges under U.S. domestic law or as necessary in the World Trade Organisation (WTO)," Trade Minister Tim Fischer and Industry Minister John Moore said in a joint statement.
The U.S. said on Tuesday it would investigate Australia, Argentina, Brazil and Indonesia under its so-called Section 301 trade law that allows retaliation against unfair practices.
In Australia's case, the U.S. was particularly concerned at the use of export subsidies on leather used in automobile upholstery.
It said Australia, Argentina and Indonesia also would be subject to a U.S. complaint to the WTO as a result of the industry programmes which it viewed as affecting U.S. carmakers.
"We have made very clear our concern that Section 301 could be used to deter competition in the U.S. automotive leather market," Fischer said.
"The U.S. action is all the more galling given the range of market access restrictions Australian exporters face into the U.S. market."
Fischer said Australia had a substantial trade imbalance with the U.S. and more than A$1.0 billion of that was the result of U.S. market access restrictions.
He added that the Australian government had already approached the U.S. about the investigations.
Moore said the government had explained that the two schemes were temporary measures and both would be phased down in the years up to 2000.
The ministers also said Australia would welcome bilateral discussions with the U.S. on the investigations.
